review: The hymn is Proverbs 8 sung to the pre-existent Wisdom: 1:1–4 is Ps 90:2 (בְּטֶרֶם הָרִים יֻלָּדוּ) with Prov 8:25–26 and Isa 40:22, 2:1–4 is Prov 8:30 (וָאֶהְיֶה שַׁעֲשֻׁעִים) with Prov 8:23 and Col 1:16, 3:1–4 is Prov 8:30–31 with John 1:14, 4:1–4 is Isa 53:3 with Ps 22:17 and John 3:16, 5:1–4 is Isa 55:8–9 with Rom 5:8, and 6:1–4 is Ps 95:6 with Eph 2:7.

The Wisdom language is kept as the print has it: 2:3 names Him חָכְמָה outright, and the payload does not soften it into 'the wise one', because the hymn is quoting Prov 8 and the New Testament reads that chapter as the Son (1 Cor 1:24).

4:4 הִגְבִּיהוּךָ, סִמְּרוּךָ — the Arabic رَفَعُوكَ سَمَّرُوك pairs 'they lifted You' with 'they nailed You'; the Hebrew keeps the two bare verbs back to back, as the print does, so the line reads as the execution notice and not as a meditation.

5:3–4 אֱמָרְךָ לַחוֹטֵא: הִנְנִי הַגֹּאֵל הֶחָבִיב — the print sets the divine speech in quotation marks; the Hebrew uses the colon before direct speech (the glossary's convention) and keeps the quotation's content as the hymn's own surprise.
